ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows consecutive integers arranged in a spiral. It can be seen that the arrow from 1 goes up to 2, and the arrow from 2 goes right to 3; afterward 3 goes down to 4, continuing to wind around. In the outer circle, 7 goes up to 8, 8 goes up to 9, 9 then goes up to 10, and 10 goes right to 11. From the figure it can be seen that 9 is located at the upper-left corner of its square ring, and from 9 to 10 is upward, from 10 to 11 is rightward. Then reason: 625 = 25^2, which is an odd square. According to the odd-square corner pattern visible in the figure, odd square numbers, like 9, are located at the upper-left corner of the corresponding square ring. Therefore 626 after 625 is above 625; then the path turns right, so 627 is to the right of 626.

method.method_draft: Use the visible odd-square corner pattern. First read the diagram: the spiral begins 1→2 upward, 2→3 rightward, then winds clockwise; the visible number 9 is at the upper-left corner of its square ring, followed by 9→10 upward and 10→11 rightward. The text asks for the relative directions among 625, 626, and 627. Since 625 = 25^2 is an odd square, it occupies the same type of upper-left ring corner as 9 in this spiral. Therefore the next number, 626, is directly above 625, and after that the path turns right, so 627 is to the right of 626.
